newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait says fall in Q2 crude oil prices possible.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait says fall in Q2 crude oil prices possible.

text.p: Weaker demand and OPEC overproduction could push down oil prices in the second quarter of 1997, Kuwait's oil minister was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

"A decline in second quarter (oil) prices is possible due to a fall in seasonal demand and expected continuation of quota violations by some OPEC members," Isa al-Mazeedi told al-Watan newspaper in an interview.
"Possible increase of Iraqi (oil) exports" is another factor, Mazeedi added without elaboration.

Kuwait's former occupier has been under United Nations sanctions since 1990 but OPEC member Iraq reached a deal last year with the United Nations to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to pay for humanitarian imports and other expenses.
Mazeedi said the expected drop in world oil prices in the second quarter "is no rule. Price levels during the second quarter in some of the previous years registered a rise."
London futures for North Sea benchmark Brent blend closed 40 cents down on Monday at $19.58 a barrel.

"A (rising) price direction is possible in line with the regular maintenance cycle of some refineries in major industrial countries...and the start of the season when demand on gasoline rises at the begining of May -- the driving season -- these reasons could preserve acceptable price levels," Mazeedi said.
"We (Kuwait) hope that OPEC countries would cooperate by adhering to the production quotas for the interest of all."
Mazeedi added that the price fall in February was "due to excess in production versus demand levels, and stocks of some products returning to their normal levels."

According to a Reuters survey, production by Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) rose 130,000 barrels per day in February to 26.77 million compared with a set ceiling of 25.033 million bpd.
Kuwait, an OPEC co-founder with a two million bpd quota, has had an average output of 2.08 million bpd over the past three months, the survey showed.
